title: UK mobile plans: PAYG, SIM-only and handset contracts
summary: Compare UK mobile plans, check coverage and costs, and switch using a PAC if you want to keep your number.
content:
# UK mobile plans: PAYG, SIM-only and handset contracts

Last updated: 2026-11-21

## Start with the phone and the plan
Pay as you go (PAYG) generally means paying in advance or topping up, often to buy a bundle. Check when the bundle expires or renews, and when inactivity could cost you your number. SIM-only supplies the service without a new phone. It can be a rolling plan or have a minimum term. A handset deal supplies a phone too. Check whether the device and airtime have separate agreements, bills and end dates.

New to the UK? Check which ID, address and payment details the provider needs. A pay-monthly plan or device finance may involve a credit check. If you already have a compatible unlocked phone, compare prepaid and monthly SIM-only options before taking on device finance. Check eSIM compatibility if relevant. See [opening a UK bank account](/en/money/open-uk-bank-account-new-arrival) and [UK credit history](/en/money/uk-credit-history-and-credit-score).

## Compare service and total cost
Check indoor and outdoor coverage at home, work and along your usual journeys. A brand may use another operator’s network. Confirm the host network and plan features such as 5G or Wi-Fi calling with the provider. A coverage map is an estimate. [Ofcom coverage map](#guide-evidence-coverage)

Add the upfront charge, airtime, device payments and listed price increases over the minimum term. Ask for the contract summary and check minimum term, cancellation charge, out-of-bundle costs and device balance. For new contracts from 17 January 2025, any rise written into the contract must be stated upfront in pounds and pence, with when it applies. [Ofcom pricing rules](#guide-evidence-price)

Check the country and your exact plan before travelling. Roaming can cost extra, even in Europe. Look for a daily fee, usage cap and fair-use limits. Near a border, check whether your phone has joined a foreign network. [Ofcom roaming guidance](#guide-evidence-roaming)

If you signed up online or by phone, there is usually a 14-day cooling-off period. You may owe for service used. Signing in a shop does not usually give the same right. Ask about any separate handset return or finance agreement. [Cancellation guidance for England](#guide-evidence-cancel)

## Switch or cancel
- Keep your number: text **PAC** to **65075**. If you want a new number and want the old service ended by the new provider, text **STAC** to **75075**.
- To check contract or exit information without requesting a switch code, text **INFO** to **85075**. For multiple numbers on one account, use your online account or contact your provider.
- Give the code to the new provider within 30 days. Once they receive it, they should arrange the switch within one working day. Check the transfer with a call and a text. If keeping the number, leave the old line active until the transfer.
- Check the old provider’s final bill and any separate device finance. Switching does not erase a balance or an early termination charge. If you only want to close a line, check cancellation directly. [Ofcom switching process](#guide-evidence-switch)

## Before ordering
Write down the places you need signal, data you normally use, full cost, term, roaming rules, exit fee and whether you need to keep your number. Save the contract summary.
